metadata.title: ePIRLS 2016 Den digitala läsförmågan hos svenska elever i årskurs 4 i ett internationellt perspektiv

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report presents descriptive and comparative results from ePIRLS 2016 (a large-scale international assessment) for Sweden and other participating countries. The provided text describes the sampling approach (two-stage selection of schools and classes/groups) and notes that ePIRLS is an international survey with statistical uncertainty, but it does not specify the exact student sampling/analysis weight variables or any replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife). The excerpt also does not report any student-level analytic dataset construction steps beyond exclusions for students unable to participate (e.g., cognitive/physical disabilities or insufficient Swedish proficiency). Because no machine-learning modeling is described in the provided text, the report’s weighting strategy cannot be verified from the excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The document is a national technical report summarizing ePIRLS 2016 results (means, confidence intervals, and subgroup comparisons) rather than an analysis that trains predictive ML models on PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. The excerpt does not describe any PV generation/combination procedure (e.g., Rubin’s rules) or any explicit missing-data handling method for an analytic model. Therefore, PV handling and missing-data handling are not documented in the provided text, representing a reporting gap for methodological transparency.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report states that ePIRLS targets students in their fourth year of schooling (Grade 4 equivalent) and uses a two-stage random representative sampling design: schools are selected first, then one or two instructional groups/classes within each selected school. All sampled students are expected to take both PIRLS and ePIRLS, with exceptions for students who cannot participate due to cognitive or physical disabilities, or for students who have been in Sweden too briefly to have sufficient Swedish proficiency to complete the assessment. For the Sweden-focused results, the excerpt specifies approximately 3,900 students from 144 schools participated in ePIRLS 2016, with an overall student response rate of 90% for ePIRLS.

data.outcome_summary: This Skolverket report summarizes ePIRLS 2016 Grade 4 results for Sweden and compares them with other participating countries. Swedish students average 559 points in digital reading, which is 13 points above the EU/OECD average (547), and only Singapore, Norway, and Ireland score higher. The report finds subgroup differences: girls score higher than boys (567 vs 552, +15), and students with higher home resources for learning score substantially higher than those with lower resources (+43 points; 589 vs 546). Migration-background differences are reported to largely disappear after accounting for socioeconomic background (home resources). The excerpt does not describe any machine-learning model training or PV/missing-data procedures, so no ML performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) are applicable here.
